narrative.overview:
rebake is a tool, not a page. A print develops in the room you are standing in, and nothing goes to a lab. One object, the `FORMAT → FORMAT` title, carries the whole job from pick to tick.

The drop zone is the first screen: wordmark, zone, All formats, footer, and no headline above it. The column then changes in place. Screens are never swapped.
keyCharacteristics: Fibre paper and black ink in light, the unlit room in dark. Both follow the system.
Colour means state, and nothing else.
The arrow is the progress bar, and it folds into the tick.

rules.name: The State Colour Rule
rules.body: Amber is working, green is done, red is error. Actions, focus and selection are ink. The only other colour on screen is the visitor's own pictures.

rules.name: The Negative Rule
rules.body: The drop effect has no colour. The zone becomes its own negative, ink spreading from the pointer. With a file open, the Add files row fills with ink the same way.

dos: Do keep native inputs as the real controls. Range, radio and checkbox stay in place, transparent, so the keyboard, assistive tech and saved state keep working.
donts: Don't put style attributes or `<style>` in markup. The CSP has no `style-src`, so `default-src 'self'` blocks them. Script may still set `element.style`, and the springs depend on it.
Don't add an accent, or colour the drop effect.
Don't give the zone a dashed outline. The arrow's dotted track stays: it marks the distance left.
Don't set Hanken Grotesk outside 400–600. The file stops there and synthesis is off.
